source: Sandbox landmarks, not a course or IALA navigation marks. Positions are world x (east) and z (south) in metres. The bay buoys are named by their bearing from Westcove Harbour's departure (-1740, 760) and set 0.65-1.1 km out in 10-21 m of water, at least 6.9 m deep everywhere within 150 m: N up the west shore (upwind for the default wind from the north), NE off the south side of Great Holm, E out across the bay, SE and S on the way to Westcove's south shore. H1 and H2 are a harbour pair inside Westcove's basin (dredged 4.5 m) for a first short course: on one north-south line two thirds of the way from the quay face (x -1840) to the mole head (x -1650), 60 m apart and centred on the pontoon fingers (z 783), so about 90 m past the finger tips and 49 m clear of the mole (TUNING GUESS, to be playtested); white bodies told apart by their sphere and cone topmarks. VISUAL ESTIMATE sizes, distinctive colours/topmarks and painted IDs for milestone 6 sighting and chart identification. TUNING GUESS proximityRadius: a boat within 15 m of a buoy is near it, about 3.5 boat lengths (the Laser is 4.2 m), so a buoy counts only when sailed close to, and H1 and H2 (60 m apart) are clearly separate marks.
